articles.title: Logitech’s new haptics-based gaming mouse is a little better and $20 more
articles.summary: Logitech has followed up its haptics-based X2 Superstrike with a sequel with better battery life, a more responsive sensor, and slightly higher price.
articles.body: The G Pro Superstrike mouse is one of Logitech’s most interesting products. Unlike other gaming mice, it has haptic actuators beneath its two main buttons instead of mechanical switches, which decreases latency and allows for a custom click feel (the click can be super subtle, more jolty, or turned off entirely). The tech debuted in the G Pro X2 Superstrike in February, and there’s already a sequel. Well, it’s more like a 1.5 rather than a true successor. The G Pro X3 Superstrike is out October 6th for $199.99, and comes in a bold pink (as pictured) or black color scheme. The X2 will remain available at $179.99. The notable improvements with the new model include a more responsive sensor, increased battery life, and improved weight distribution. For casual gamers, the boosts are incremental and, unless you’re a pro, perhaps inconsequential to your gaming experience. The X3 supports up to 8,000Hz polling rate wirelessly, while the X2 could only achieve that speed when connected via a USB-C cable. It can last up to 135 hours per charge, which is a big improvement over the X2’s 90-hour claim — impressive considering the new model weighs two grams less in the US (it’s 61 grams in the EMEA version). Other changes include a Hero 2 sensor that has a higher ceiling for resolution (48K DPI versus 44K in the X2), higher acceleration (90G versus 88G in the X2), and higher max speed of 930 IPS (888 in the X2). It’s a little puzzling to see Logitech so quickly launch a follow-up to the X2 Superstrike with such small feature improvements. Though, at least it’s keeping the older (still great) model available, letting more people try out its very fun haptics-based clicks for a little less. It’s worth keeping in mind that the X2 temporarily dropped to $129.99 recently, so it’s possible we’ll see a similar deal coming soon ahead of the holidays.

articles.title: Scrapped GTA 5 Story DLC Might Have Taken the Series Overseas for the First Time in 15 Years
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 5's story DLC was seemingly going to take players to Paris, if leaked footage is anything to go by.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto 5's story DLC was seemingly going to take players to Paris, if leaked footage is anything to go by.

Last week, a slew of files and assets from GTA 5 surfaced online. This leak showed off variety of cut content, prompting Rockstar to take action and issue takedowns to creators who were showing it in their videos. One of the most interesting parts of this leak has been seeing all of the scrapped DLC, which includes a Liberty City map expansion .

Fans have also uncovered new information about the game's fabled story DLC, which was formally announced by Rockstar in 2013 with a 2014 release window in mind. Unfortunately, none of it ever saw the light of day, as Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA Online became higher priorities. One of the DLCs would've followed Trevor assuming the role of a secret agent, tackling dirty jobs for the government and assassinating powerful foes. Much of this was already known, but what fans likely weren't aware that this DLC was also seemingly going to take players to Paris.

In the leaked files, players were able to look at some of the unfinished levels made for this DLC, and one of them includes some kind of luxury apartment that overlooks Paris. The Eiffel Tower can be seen outside of a balcony, though it's just a flat image rather than an explorable 3D environment. It's entirely possible that this apartment would've been the extent of the overseas adventure, potentially being used for a cutscene or maybe some kind of assassination mission.

The only other time Grand Theft Auto has taken players overseas was in GTA: London 1969, which was an expansion for the original game released in 1999. Some fans have hoped to see the series go abroad, but the franchise's former writer and creative director, Dan Houser, suggested that the series wouldn't work as well outside of America .

"I think for a full GTA game, we always decided there was so much Americana inherent in the IP, it would be really hard to make it work in London or anywhere else," said Houser in 2025. "You know, you needed guns, you needed these larger-than-life characters. It just felt like the game was so much about America, possibly from an outsider's perspective. But that was so much about what the thing was that it wouldn't really have worked in the same way elsewhere.”

Trevor actor Steven Ogg has spoken loosely about the scrapped GTA 5 story DLC in the past. He shot some scenes for it, but Rockstar never followed up on the project, and that was the end of it. A former developer estimated that the DLC was about halfway finished when the plug was pulled and was sour about its cancellation.

“It was really really good," said ex-Rockstar Senior Camera Artist Joe Robino. "But when GTA Online came out, it was so much of a cash cow and people were loving it so much that it was hard to make an argument that a standalone DLC would outcompete that. I think looking back now you could probably do both. But that was a business decision they made. I was a little upset about that. That actually was a lot of the reason for me being a little sour at that time. Because I was like yo, WTF guys? This s**t’s awesome. Let’s keep going. Let’s finish this s**t.”

With GTA 6 on the horizon, it seems unlikely we'll ever see this DLC revived, but some of it was salvaged into GTA Online updates like The Doomsday Heist.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: After Asking Very Nicely For a Skin, Madison Beer Joins Fortnite Tomorrow
articles.summary: Madison Beer is the latest music icon to join the world of Fortnite, after previously issuing a public call to Epic Games for her to become a skin.
articles.body:
Madison Beer is the latest music icon to join the world of Fortnite , after previously issuing a public call to Epic Games for her to become a skin.

The Selfish and Make You Mine singer has long been a fan of Epic Games' battle royale, and has helped promote some of its LEGO-focused modes. Now, Beer is pulling up her socks to join the core Fortnite experience, following her callout to be included — made during an episode of the Hot Ones podcast earlier this year.

Beer follows in the footsteps of other pop icons such as Sabrina Carpenter, Ariana Grande, and Olivia Rodrigo, as well as a swathe of other musical artists including Billie Eilish, Lady Gaga, Eminem and Snoop Dogg, all of whom have multiple in-game skins.

This latest addition will see Beer gain two skins, one of which is themed after her 2025 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show appearance, plus a pickaxe, backblings, emotes, a gun skin, microphone instrument, a loading screen and three more in-game tracks: "yes, baby," "bittersweet," and "complexity."

"I would say this is definitely up there with being nominated for a Grammy and playing Madison Square Garden," Beer said in a statement today. "There's things in my life that I am just obsessed with, and that I would die for, and Fortnite is one of them."

Madison Beer lands in the Fortnite shop tomorrow, and will be streaming the game via Twitch on Friday to celebrate her collaboration finally happening. Who will join Fortnite next?

articles.title: How to Watch Dragon Ball in Order: Series, Sagas, and Movies
articles.summary: From the mind of the legendary Akira Toriyama, the Dragon Ball timeline includes seven anime series and over twenty movies and specials. Here's how to watch it all in order.
articles.body:
It's easy to underestimate just how influential the Dragon Ball franchise is, but the Akira Toriyama manga essentially defined what an action shonen manga would be for the next 40 years. Goku became the archetypical anime protagonist , while his relationship with Vegeta became the standard that all anime rivalries would emulate. It helped popularize power-up transformations, time jumps, and much more in both anime and manga.

Sure, it's easy to boil down Dragon Ball to just having extremely long fight scenes, but the franchise is much more than that. With bold changes in tone, from hilarious gag comedy to meaningful moments of inspiration, as well as a myriad of great side characters, Dragon Ball remains as good as its reputation would suggest.

Still, this is one of the longest-running anime franchises, with dozens of movies in addition to several anime series. It can be hard to navigate the Dragon Ball universe, but that's what this guide is for. Whether you fell off the wagon at one point and want to catch up, or you're looking to embark on your very first journey with Son Goku, here's how to watch every Dragon Ball anime and movie in order.

Inspired by Akira Toriyama's manga of the same name, Dragon Ball includes over 800 episodes across five anime series. There have also been over 20 anime movies set in the Dragon Ball universe, which expand the story or even continue it.

Now, what about canon? That's where it gets a bit complicated. Granted, Toriyama never really cared much about canon, as he constantly tinkered with his story, retconning things whenever he thought of something better than he had before (remember when Goku was just a happy monkey guy and not an alien superhero?). Still, what makes Dragon Ball canon complicated is that while most of the movies aren't technically canon, the last four movies are part of the official Dragon Ball continuity.

Then there's Dragon Ball Daima , a canon anime series that seemed to make Dragon Ball GT , a show long considered to be non-canon, somewhat canon. So what does this mean? Well, it is kind of up to the audience. If you like Dragon Ball GT, then you can think of it as canon. If you prefer to skip it, then by all means, do so.

The full scope of everything Dragon Ball is on Crunchyroll . The anime streaming service is also the only place you'll find most of the movies, though Z Kai and Daima are also streaming on Hulu. For the collectors, all of the Dragon Ball series and movies are available as physical releases.

Dragon Ball Z: Collection One (Movies 1 to 5)

2. Dragon Ball: Curse of the Blood Rubies (Movie)

An alternate retelling of the first saga of the story. Best watched after the Emperor Pilaf Saga rather than have this be your first exposure to the characters.

4. Dragon Ball: Sleeping Princess in Devil's Castle (Movie)

Goku and Krillin are tasked to save a sleeping princess from Lucifer (yes, that Lucifer). The movie takes place at the start of Goku and Krillin's training.

6. Dragon Ball: Mystical Adventure (Movie)

Goku and Krillin join the World Martial Arts Tournament while Bora hides a Dragon Ball from the emperor's evil forces.

7. Dragon Ball: The Path to Power (Movie)

An alternate retelling of the story so far, merging the first two sagas with some cool changes.

Garlic Jr. kidnaps Gohan, so Goku must rescue his son.

12. Dragon Ball Z: Bardock – The Father of Goku (Special)

A prequel showing the final days of the planet Vegeta before Frieza destroyed it, focusing on Goku's father, Bardock.

14. Dragon Ball Z: The World's Strongest (Movie)

Goku and his friends must defeat an evil scientist who kidnaps Bulma, but when Gohan shows his incredible power, the scientist tries to steal his body!

15. Dragon Ball Z: The Tree of Might (Movie)

We have pirates now! A Sayian pirate called Turles and his crew attempt to conquer the Earth by planting a magical tree that can absorb all life on the planet and leave it a desolated wasteland.

What if Dragon Ball was Michael Bay's Armageddon? This time, Earth is threatened by a massive asteroid on a collision course towards Earth. While Krillin and Goku head out to stop it, a Namekian conqueror tries to use the Dragon Balls to take over Earth.

18. Dragon Ball Z: The History of Trunks (Special)

A special depicting the post-apocalyptic future that Trunks comes from, and how the sword-wielding teenager went back in time to prevent his future from existing.

20. Dragon Ball Z: Cooler's Revenge (Movie)

Goku and his friends go on a camping trip after the defeat of Frieza, but their celebrations are interrupted when the alien conqueror's older brother comes looking for revenge.

22. Dragon Ball Z: Super Android 13 (Movie)

New terrifying murder androids, 13, 14, and 15 are activated after Android 17 and 18 murder Dr. Gero. Now, Goku and the Z Fighters must deal with them.

Cooler is back, and now he's a robot! After enslaving the people of New Namek, Cooler arrives on Earth with an army of robots. Making matters worse, the world-be conqueror claims to have killed Goku.

25. Dragon Ball Z: Broly – The Legendary Super Saiyan

The Z Fighters are invited to the planet New Vegeta. There, they catch wind of a legendary Super Saiyan hellbent on destroying the universe.

Gohan finally gets the spotlight! The demon Bojack is finally free, and he decides to host the biggest martial arts tournament in the galaxy, and Gohan is the only one capable of saving the Earth.

29. Dragon Ball Z: Broly – Second Coming (Movie)

Broly is back, awakened by Goten's crying (yes, this actually happened). This movie is memorable for having a Father-Sons Kamehameha with Gohan, Goten and Goku's spirit.

Yes, Broly is still somehow around, and he returns yet again as a clone. Goten, Trunks, and best boy Krillin have to stop him.

32. Dragon Ball Z: Fusion Reborn (Movie)

A fever dream of a movie, featuring villains long dead. Worth watching because of Vegeta and Goku's fusion form, but generally part of its own timeline.

33. Dragon Ball Z: Wrath of the Dragon (Movie)

The gang fights a kaiju in this movie, which has some of the best music in the franchise.

The not-quite canon Dragon Ball series originally aired after Dragon Ball Z and is generally considered to be a part of its own timeline. Emperor Pilaf uses the Black Star Dragon Ball to turn Goku into a child.

The most recent Dragon Ball series follows Goku and friends who have been turned into children and must traverse the Demon Realm to become adults again.

The next two Dragon Ball Z movies (Battle of the Gods and Resurrection F) and the first two sagas of Dragon Ball Super cover the same general storylines, but with some key differences. The Dragon Ball Super sagas are considered canon, but it's worth checking both out.

37. Dragon Ball Z: Battle of the Gods (Movie)

This is the movie where Goku fights a literal god, and all arguments about who can and can't defeat Goku become forever pointless.

39. Dragon Ball Z: Resurrection F (Movie)

No one ever dies in Dragon Ball, so of course Frieza comes back to life and swears revenge on Goku. That's it. That's the movie. Oh, and Vegeta gets a cool new power.

The film tells the story of Broly and his history with Goku, Raditz and Vegeta. In the present, Broly returns yet again to wreak havoc, and it is up to Goku and Vegeta to literally combine forces to stop him.

42. Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero (Movie)

The best father-son duo, Piccolo and Gohan, finally get the spotlight! We also get the triumphant return of the Red Ribbon Army, who create androids to take over the world.

I wouldn't recommend splitting up Dragon Ball Z like this on your first watch, but the original ending saga technically takes place 10 years after the defeat of Majin Buu. At the very least, it may be worth coming back to these final episodes after watching Dragon Ball Super.

It’s been 8 years, but Dragon Ball Super is finally set to return. At a recent Dragon Ball 40th anniversary event , it was announced that Dragon Ball Super will return with The Galactic Patrol, an anime adaptation of the Galactic Patrol Prisoner Arc. It will follow Goku and Vegeta teaming up to capture the nefarious Moro. Though we don’t know when The Galactic Patrol will premiere, we also got the announcement that Dragon Ball Super: Beerus – a remake of the first arc of Dragon Ball Super – is set to be released in Fall 2026.

Outside of animation, we recently learned that we'll be getting Dragon Ball-themed LEGO sets . The franchise also released a collaboration with Converse earlier this year.

Rafael Motamayor is a contributing freelancer for IGN covering everything anime and animation.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Shirts Given Away for Free at Tokyo Game Show Are Being Resold Online for Hundreds of Dollars
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 shirts that were given away for free exclusively at Tokyo Game Show 2026 are already being resold online for hundreds of dollars.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto 6 shirts that were given away for free exclusively at Tokyo Game Show 2026 are already being resold online for hundreds of dollars.

Attendees at Tokyo Game Show who got the chance to participate in a special immersive screening for GTA 6’s viral Netflix special were treated to commemorative T-shirts to celebrate the occasion.

This screening was the exact same extended trailer that launched on Netflix last month, but with more bells and whistles; it featured tricks like surround sound and 4D haptic effects that correlated with what was happening on screen, letting viewers feel like they were actually tagging along with Jason and Lucia as they fled from the fuzz and held up corner stores.

Even More GTA 6 Screenshots from Rockstar Games

The experience was so popular that the GTA 6 booth closed after just 10 minutes , having already reached capacity — but savvy fans saw an opportunity to capitalize on the overwhelming demand and make some quick cash.

As spotted by Dexerto , the commemorative T-shirts handed out by PlayStation at the game's TGS 2026 booth for free have already made their way online and are being resold on platforms like eBay for hundreds of dollars.

A quick browse on eBay shows a handful of listings pricing the shirts around $140 - $200, while other goodies that were given out at Rockstar’s booth, like GTA 6-branded stickers and carabiners , are being marked up to the tune of $30 - $40.

This isn’t a new phenomenon, by far; exclusive merchandise like this has become a target for scalpers across several big franchises over the last few years. One Piece’s viral collaboration with Popeye’s is a prime example of this, as scalpers waited in lines that trailed blocks away from their local fast food franchises to snag special Luffy-themed bento boxes, only to list them online for staggeringly high prices.

The same can be said of the Pokemon Trading Card scene; scalpers have become ravenous for Pokemon card packs and merchandise, causing chaos at retailers and even sparking violent confrontations that have ended in arrests.

The hype for GTA 6 is at an all-time high, so we can’t say that these shirts getting resold online is a huge surprise. The city of Miami is even working with Rockstar on some special advertising for the game, having recently erected a massive, $1 million 'Welcome to Vice City' sign after entering talks with officials for a possible GTA 6-themed takeover of the entire area .

articles.title: Tolkien's Silmarillion Illustrated Edition Drops to Its Lowest Price Ever for Amazon Prime Members
articles.body:
If you're a Tolkien fan, you likely know that there's always more lore to discover. That's where the Silmarillion comes in. Unlike the other Lord of the Rings books that focus on narrative storytelling, the Silmarillion is a deep dive into the mythology and history that defines Middle Earth. It's an essential look into the fantasy world J.R.R. Tolkien so lovingly created.

The Silmarillion is available in multiple versions, but the illustrated editions offer the best overall experience thanks to maps, drawings, and more from Tolkien himself. If you're interested in learning more about Middle Earth straight from the source, Amazon is currently discounting the collector's edition to its lowest price ever ahead of Prime Big Deal Days .

If you're not already familiar with what the Silmarillion actually is, here's a quick rundown: This book covers the early history of its fictional universe, Eä, and the various lands it contains. This includes Valinor, Beleriand, Númenor, and, of course, Middle-Earth. Broken up into five distinct parts, readers can expect deep lore exposition, extensive historical accounts of the First Age, and summaries of the Third Age stories we know and love, the Lord of the Rings.

The illustrated edition itself is 432 pages long and includes the complete text of the Silmarillion alongside full-color prints of Tolkien's illustrations. It also includes two removable fold-out maps. It's essentially a deep dive into the inner workings of one of the best-selling fantasy franchises of all time.

The Hobbit Illustrated Edition has also dropped to its lowest price ever . More premium "Deluxe" editions are currently on sale, but not at record-breaking prices. These prices are the best we've seen in 2026 so far, though, so it's worth picking up any of these editions if you're on the hunt for a good Lord of the Rings gift at a discount.

This upcoming special edition is actually illustrated by Alan Lee rather than only featuring art from Tolkien himself.

articles.title: 4 Burning Doomsday Questions We Have After Avengers: Endgame Encore
articles.summary: The new scenes from Avengers: Endgame Encore have leaked online, and they raise some very interesting questions about the plot of Avengers: Doomsday. Let's break it all down.
articles.body:
Marvel is about to release Avengers: Endgame Encore in theaters. Not only is this a chance to rewatch the climax of the Infinity Saga on the big screen again, it also gives fans several new scenes to chew on. Each of these scenes is meant to create connective tissue with Avengers: Doomsday and lay the groundwork for the debut of Robert Downey, Jr.’s Doctor Doom.

Those scenes have now leaked onto the Internet ahead of Endgame Encore’s release [Note - we’re pretty confident these leaks are genuine, but you can never be 100% sure in the age of AI.]. And there’s definitely a lot of food for thought here. We see key TVA figures reacting to the impending collapse of the multiverse and Doom himself kicking off some sort of recruiting spree. These scenes raise more questions than they answer about the plot of Doomsday, so let’s break down what we do and don’t know right now.

Avengers: Doomsday Trailer: First Look at Doctor Doom

In what is easily the most intriguing new addition to Endgame, we get a scene focused on Mark Ruffalo’s Bruce Banner set in the aftermath of Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Banner has clearly seen better days, as he’s still recovering from the physical and psychological trauma of being hijacked by Sadie Sink’s Jean Grey . He’s desperate to reassert control over his Hulk persona, and so he’s locked himself deep in an underground bunker to test a new “gamma suppression system.”

But no sooner does Banner begin his test than the lights flicker and a certain armored villain makes his presence known. We hear (but don’t see) Downey’s Doom, who proclaims “I’ve come to collect you.” Both men then vanish, leaving only a glowing green rune on the ground (similar to the ones left when Asgardians travel on the Rainbow Bridge).

So the obvious question here is what Doom wants with Banner. He seems to be building some sort of team, but to what end? Is he more interested in Banner’s brains or Hulk’s brawn? We’d guess the former, as past movies have already set up the character as a voice of authority in the growing multiverse crisis. And judging from the Doomsday trailers and the fact that Doom can deflect Thor’s mighty Stormbreaker with ease, we doubt he’s in need of any extra muscle.

Is Doom assembling his own team of Avengers here? If so, what other characters might he be recruiting? Is it possible he’s building a version of the Illuminati as a brain trust to deal with Incursions? In the lead-up to the 2015 Secret Wars comic, the Illuminati also included members like Iron Man, Mister Fantastic, Beast, Namor, Black Panther, and Black Bolt. Doom himself wasn’t a member of that team, but he was working toward similar goals and forged his own alliances. Will the MCU Doom seek these heroes out on Earth-616?

Or is Doom planning for a post-multiverse future here? We have to wonder if Downey’s character has already given up on saving reality as it currently exists and is building his Battleworld contingency plan. Perhaps he wants Banner to serve as one of the barons on Battleworld (a role that a version of Hulk did fill in the comic).

Whatever the case, it seems that Ruffalo has a bigger part to play in Avengers: Doomsday than we realized. Ruffalo wasn’t even part of the initial cast chair announcement . But if there’s one takeaway from Avengers: Endgame Encore, it’s that Doomsday’s cast is going to be even bigger than we thought.

Another new scene shows us the current state of things at the TVA, as Mr. Mobius (Owen Wilson), Casey (Eugene Cordero), and Ouroboros (Ke Huy Quan) confront the rapidly deteriorating situation with the multiverse. They can only watch their charmingly low-res computer displays as worlds begin colliding and some Earths declare all-out war on each other. By the end of the scene, it’s reported that no fewer than 3000 Incursions are happening simultaneously. One of those looks to be Earth-10005, the home of Fox’s X-Men.

This scene makes it clear that, even with Marvel pivoting away from Jonathan Majors’ Kang the Conqueror as the central villain of the Multiverse Saga, the Loki series is going to be an important precursor to Doomsday. That series chronicled the rebirth of the multiverse and placed Tom Hiddleston’s redeemed Loki at the heart of creation . But no sooner has the multiverse been restored than it’s started to come apart at the seams.

Why is that, exactly? What’s the root cause of the multiverse’s collapse and the threat of Incursions? Why does it seem to be happening all at once rather than gradually? Is this why Doom is suddenly making his presence known on Earth-616?

This scene may hold an important clue. Early on, we hear TVA mascot Miss Minutes (Tara Strong) reminding her employees that it’s essential for all beings to remain within their home universes for the sake of existence. Unfortunately, there’s one pivotal character who doesn’t seem to have followed the rules.

What Is Loki Doing at Steve and Peggy’s House?

Endgame Encore puts the heartwarming ending of the original Endgame in a very different context. This time, the film lingers longer with the dancing Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) and Peggy Carter (Hayley Atwell), as a tender kiss is interrupted by a knock at the door. Steve quickly hides while Peggy answers, only to realize the person at the door is none other than Loki.

We can infer from Loki’s TVA attire that this is a version of the character from sometime in the middle of the Loki series. He’s committed to the TVA’s mission, but hasn’t yet taken his place atop the multiversal throne. And echoing Miss Minutes’ warning broadcast, we can only assume that Loki has come to tell Steve that he’s violating the laws of existence by travelling back in time to be with Peggy.

That said, we don’t think Loki is there to force Steve to return to his rightful place and time. Obviously, Steve has remained MIA in the present-day MCU ever since journeying back in time with the Infinity Stones. And we know from the very first Doomsday trailer that Steve and Peggy remain together long enough to raise a baby together. By the time Steve does reunite with the Avengers in Doomsday, he’s clearly older and sporting his beard again.

So what exactly is Loki’s intention here? Has he found some loophole that will allow Steve to remain in the past with Peggy? If so, why is he so committed to letting one man violate the basic laws of the TVA? Is it just his way of thanking Steve for helping to restore the lives Thanos took?

Most importantly, does this mean Captain America is the catalyst causing all these Incursions? Given Miss Minutes’ ominous warning, we have to assume that Steve’s decision to do something for himself for a change has cost the multiverse dearly.

Hot Toys Avengers: Doomsday Victor von Doom Figure

What Is the Significance of Doom’s Armor?

Avengers: Endgame Encore wraps with one final addition to the original film. Endgame originally had no post-credits scenes (a rarity for the MCU, to be sure). All it had to offer fans who stuck around through the credits was the sound of a hammer striking metal, a callback to Downey’s Tony Stark forging his original suit of armor in 2008’s Iron Man.

But here again, Encore presents this ending in a very different context. This version ends with that same sound, but this time we see Doom forging his metal mask. It’s a fun way of subverting the original Endgame, and it almost tricks you into believing that introducing Doom was the plan way back in 2019.

Apart from ending Encore on a fitting note, this scene does highlight one particular question. What is the actual significance of Doom’s armor? Why is he wearing it in the first place? We can see from the trailers and the aforementioned Hulk scene that Doom is gifted with immense magical abilities, so why is it so important that he also be decked out in a technologically advanced suit?

In the comics, of course, Doom used the armor to hide his scarred face. Is he masking similar injuries here? Based on one of the Doomsday posters and Vanessa Kirby’s dialogue in the second trailer , we’re assuming Doom is also mourning the deaths of his family. Does the armor somehow tie back to that tragedy? The presence of a sash on his left arm (a relic of his late wife?) certainly seems to suggest so.

Answers to these questions will have to wait until Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18. Until then, let us know your theories about the new Avengers: Endgame Encore footage in the comments below.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

articles.title: Crocodile Dundee Is Getting a 4K Steelbook Edition for Its 40th Anniversary
articles.summary: Crocodile Dundee, the 1980s blockbuster hit, is getting the 4K steelbook treatment in honor of its 40th anniversary.
articles.body:
Crocodile Dundee, the 1986 box office hit, is getting the 4K steelbook treatment. The movie will be available December 1 for $39.99, but it’s available now for preorder at Amazon . I, for one, am excited.

It may be hard to imagine now, in an era when theatrical releases for comedies are few and far between, but there was a period during the 1980s when Crocodile Dundee was king. The character, played by Paul Hogan, was a pop culture icon. That’s because this movie was a mega-hit.

Crocodile Dundee - Steelbook Edition (4K UHD + Digital)

Made for under $10 million, Crocodile Dundee grossed $328 million worldwide, landing it at number two on the list of highest-grossing movies of 1986, behind only Top Gun . That’s a remarkable feat for a movie about an Outback outdoorsman.

Crocodile Dundee works because it’s a mix of tried-and-true ideas: It’s a fish-out-of-water story and a romance between an unlikely couple. It starts when Sue Charlton (Linda Kozlowski), a New York journalist, travels to the Australian Outback and meets the titular hero, a hunter who feels more at home in the wilderness than he does around other people.

Soon Sue invites Croc to come back to NYC with her. He agrees, and plenty of comedic hijinks ensue as Dundee’s outdoorsy sensibilities clash with city living. Cue Sue’s gradual romantic feelings toward Dundee, and her ambivalence about her current boyfriend.

The movie spawned a less-revered sequel in 1988, followed over a decade later by 2001’s Crocodile Dundee in Los Angeles. I’m not sure how well the original movie holds up, because I haven’t seen it since the VHS era, but I’m hopeful it still plays. I remember enjoying it a lot (and quoting it a lot) as a kid.

If you enjoy classic movies from decades ago, you have plenty of other options as well. Hook is getting a 35th anniversary steelbook edition . Shrek is getting a 25th anniversary steelbook . And plenty of others have big discounts in Amazon’s early Prime Big Deal Days sale .

articles.title: Game of Thrones Star Kit Harington Isn't a Gamer, but He's Excited for Grand Theft Auto 6
articles.summary: Game of Thrones star Kit Harington has confessed that he isn't much of a gamer, but wants to play Grand Theft Auto 6.
articles.body:
Game of Thrones star Kit Harington has confessed that he isn't much of a gamer, but wants to play Grand Theft Auto 6 .

The actor best known for playing Jon Snow reflected on his experience with the gaming world with Josh Horowitz in a recent interview . After recalling his experience working on Silent Hill: Revelation, a live-action film based on the beloved horror gaming franchise, he was asked if he was much of a gamer. Harington noted he didn't have much experience with the Silent Hill games, but played a bit of Tekken, Mario Kart, Diddy Kong Racing, and most recently, Hogwarts Legacy.

When Horowitz asked if he'd ever dabbled in Grand Theft Auto, Harington said that he wants to play Grand Theft Auto 6 after seeing some of the advertising. He went on to express an admiration for videos that mimic GTA's tropes in real life. All of this sort of goes to show that the GTA 6 effect is beginning to happen, as even non-gamers are getting pulled in by its trance.

Even More GTA 6 Screenshots from Rockstar Games

Rockstar is spending a boatload of cash to get the game in front of as many people as possible. It has assembled an Avengers-level ensemble of musicians to craft an original soundtrack for Grand Theft Auto 6, spent nearly $1 million on a "Welcome to Vice City" sign in Miami , and is likely only going to continue to ramp things up as we get closer to launch. NBA star Steven Adams also joked that he expects the performance of the league to drop when GTA 6 releases in November.

As for Harington specifically, he didn't say whether or not he will actually end up playing GTA 6 or not. He's had some experience in the gaming world, as he was the main antagonist in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare and voiced Jon Snow in Telltale's Game of Thrones video game. His next big role will be playing Gildroy Lockhart in HBO's Harry Potter TV series, which may explain why he recently dabbled in Hogwarts Legacy.

articles.title: The Grond LEGO Set Is Free When You Buy LEGO Lord of the Rings Minas Tirith
articles.summary: LEGO has brought back the Grond battering ram set as a free Gift with Purchase when you buy the massive LEGO Lord of the Rings Minas Tirith.
articles.body:
It’s back. LEGO has brought back LEGO Lord of the Rings Grond , a 307-piece set based on the wolf-shaped battering ram the Orcs use to shatter the Great Gate of Minas Tirith in the Battle of the Pelennor Fields. It’s an awesome-looking set, and between now and September 30 it’s free – in a manner of speaking. There’s only one catch: to get it, you have to buy the $650 LEGO Minas Tirith set from the LEGO Store . I’m sorry.

Get Grond Free with LEGO The Lord of the Rings: Minas Tirith

LEGO The Lord of the Rings: Minas Tirith

Grond is what LEGO calls a Gift with Purchase” or “GWP.” These are smaller free sets LEGO gives you When you buy select sets from the official LEGO Store . GWPs are limited edition, and are not available to purchase separately. The problem is, they’re only available for a limited time, and LEGO often runs out of stock before that time is up.

Sometimes, however, LEGO brings them back. That’s the case with Grond. The Grond set is available once again, while supplies last, as a Minas Tirith GWP until September 30. As is fitting for any GWP accompanying the mammoth Minas Tirith set, Grond isn’t actually all that small. Valued at $29.99, it has you build a rolling support structure as well as the beastly, flame-throwing battering ram. It also includes two weapon-wielding Orc minifigures.

Minas Tirith, meanwhile, is a 8,278-piece behemoth, the largest LEGO Lord of the Rings set ever released. Kevin Wong , our go-to LEGO expert, built this gorgeous set and wrote about the experience, concluding, “It receives our highest recommendation.”

If you do buy the pricy Minas Tirith set, you’ll also get another GWP set in addition to Grond. That’s LEGO Scary Haunted Tree (which comes with all orders of $100 or more). If you enter an exclusive code found over on The Brick Fan at checkout, you might even be able to get LEGO Ideas Friendly Snails for free as well. articles.title: The Conjuring Gets Its First-Ever Video Game Coming to Netflix Next Month
articles.summary: The Conjuring is coming to Netflix in the form of a video game, marking the franchise’s first foray into the medium after releasing ten films over the last decade.
articles.body:
The Conjuring is coming to Netflix in the form of a video game, marking the franchise’s first foray into the medium after releasing ten films over the last decade.

Titled The Conjuring: Unspoken, the game is slated to launch on the streamer this October. As spotted by Polygon , this news was announced unceremoniously in the platform’s monthly New on Netflix newsletter, which had only a small blurb to share about what players can expect from this latest entry in Ed and Lorraine Warren’s ghostly adventures.

“What is haunting the Red Lion Inn? Scan for paranormal signals and investigate the eerie events troubling a grieving family in this cinematic game,” the blurb reads.

The Conjuring Movies in (Chronological) Order

Thus far, anything else about the game is unknown; we aren’t sure if it’ll mimic Netflix’s most recent horror game, Unhinged , which was a first-person, interactive title featuring a celebrity cast including Zoë Kravitz and Sadie Sink, or if it’ll be something completely different.

We don’t even know if Ed or Lorraine will be in the game at all, though it would seem odd if they weren’t, as the blurb makes it seem like the pair is going off on one of their iconic paranormal investigations again.

What we do know is that, unlike other games under Netflix’s umbrella, it’ll be a cloud-based title, presumably not tied to mobile devices or any particular platform. It's also cinematic, meaning that it'll almost certainly contain grand cutscenes and a heavy narrative focus.

This marks The Conjuring’s very first fully-dedicated video game adaptation, and it’s coming right in time for spooky season. While an exact launch date has not yet been shared, it’ll release on the heels of Silent Hill: Townfall , the second title from Konami’s horror series that’s released in the last two years. It’s received rave reviews thus far, with IGN scoring the game an 8 out of 10 — so it looks like Untold has its work cut out for it if it hopes to catch players’ attention.

The Conjuring has been featured in another game, though; Fortnite notably included a map themed after The Conjuring: Last Rites , in 2025.

Last Rites is the newest film in the famous horror series first kicked off by James Wan in 2013, and the final story in ‘phase one’ of its overarching narrative. Another installment is releasing in 2027 titled The Conjuring: First Communion, though details on this movie are also slim at the moment.

Cloud-based gaming is a big focus for Netflix at the moment, thanks to the success of Unhinged this summer. “We're scratching the surface in terms of what we think the total potential of the space offers for us,” co-CEO Greg Peters told investors in a July 2026 call . “You're going to see us continue to calibrate and refine our level of investment here, which is still very small relative to our overall content spend based on demonstrated performance based on what is working for our members and what's delivering returns to our business.”

We just hope that the studio making The Conjuring: Untold doesn’t get shuttered like Unhinged’s developer, Nightschool, did, despite being responsible for one of the steamer’s “most successful cloud game debuts” ever.

articles.title: Halo Fans Are Divided Over Whether Activision Should Reboot the Series and Start Fresh
articles.summary: Halo fans are divided on whether or not Activision should completely reboot the franchise or keep Master Chief's story going.
articles.body:
Halo fans are divided on whether or not Activision should completely reboot the franchise or keep Master Chief's story going.

A rumor floating around the internet from a user named TechnicalHalo suggests that Activision will totally reboot the series, throwing all of the lore out the window in favor of a fresh start. We advise you take this with a grain of salt, as we have no idea what Activision's plans are for Halo, but it has started an interesting conversation among fans. Should Activision use its first Halo game to create a clean slate for the beloved sci-fi franchise?

A segment of fans are under the impression that, although Halo has gone off the rails in the last decade, there are still some elements from the newer games that are worth keeping. Bungie's contributions to the franchise (Halo: Campaign Evolved through Halo: Reach) are valued by fans, so some believe that if there's a way to retcon Halo 4 and onwards, that would be a valid option, as well. This ensures that the most beloved Chief stories remain canon, while also giving Activision an option to tell a whole new era of stories in the Halo universe.

"I’m against a full reboot," said one fan on Reddit . "But if they said the Bungie era is canon and everything else going forward is being rebooted, I wouldn’t be very upset. Halo 4 has grown on me over the yearsm but 5 and Infinite’s story led nowhere."

"My only other idea for getting back to a good status quo, short of scorching everything, would be to just do what Terminator does all the time and just start from Halo 3 again. But it would basically nullify any investment people had in the last decade+, even if it wasn't much, and still give the impression there's no direction if you cop out on a true follow-up," said another .

That same fan suggested the idea of a full blown reboot might be born out of necessity, given Master Chief actor Steve Downes is getting older and will inevitably need to be recast if they want to tell new stories with the character.

"Steve Downes I just don't think is a long-term option for Chief anymore at his age and a recast is inevitable. You can keep Taylor as Cortana and the Campaign Evolved recasts but a reboot would immediately clear the deck for new versions of the characters and new actors. I'm actually more interested in a full reboot at this point than even a loose Infinite sequel. A full reboot actually sounds like more of a plan," they added.

Another fan echoed these sentiments of recasting Chief: "Honestly might be a good call, even if a lot of Halo fans hate the idea," said another fan. "If they’re wanting to grow the franchise again and get new eyes why saddle this fresh beginning with over 20 years of games, comics, and books. Plus, Steve Downes ain’t getting any younger and will probably be 80 by the time this game releases. Might be time to consider a new voice actor, and trying to recast Chief in a sequel feels like sacrilege."

Some think it's time to leave Chief behind altogether, regardless of how Activision handles the timeline, and embrace other stories in the Halo universe, similar to Halo 3: ODST and Halo: Reach.

"Reboot? Okay thats fine," one fan said . "Just make it a Halo reboot and not Master Chief reboot. Give me Halo games with new characters akin to Reach or ODST."

"I think it would be a shame to completely overwrite everything after Halo 3 since there is some good stuff there in the storylines told outside of the games," said another fan . "I think the best bet would be to just leave the current storyline as is and go either forward or backwards in the timeline and tell new stories with new characters that are mostly disconnected from what came before."

It was confirmed yesterday that Activision would be building a new team to make the next Halo game , while Halo Studios was gutted by layoffs. It's unclear if any of the Call of Duty studios will be assisting on the project, as Sledgehammer Games has long been rumored to be eyeing the Halo franchise. It will likely be a while before the next Halo materializes, especially if Activision is throwing everything out and starting from scratch. Only time will tell what happens, but it'll be interesting to see what direction they take it in regardles.

articles.title: Slow Horses Season 6 Brings Back a Fan-Favorite Character in a Shocking Episode 2 Ending (Even if We Already Knew It Was Coming)
articles.summary: Apple TV had spoiled the end of Episode 2, "Daddy Issues," in its first and only trailer. Sure woulda been a lot cooler if it hadn't.
articles.body:
This review contains full spoilers for Slow Horses Season 6, Episode 2, which is streaming on Apple TV now.

The thing we knew was happening from the first and only Season 6 trailer has happened: Olivia Cooke’s Sidonie Baker has popped back into the picture. The reappearance of the short-lived slow horse was hardly anything — that single “hello, River” line before the end credits roll — and yet raises so many questions. How is she alive? Why has she been in hiding? Why was she playing the spoof-call “triangulation” game with River? What’s she doing in his dead grandad’s house? Most importantly, why did Apple TV spoil this in the trailer?

It’s tough not to imagine how much more of an impact Sid’s return would have had if it had been saved for a jaw-dropping tag at the very last second of this episode. (I’m jealous of those who look at the internet less than me; and yes, I have reconciled with the fact that I am part of the problem . Have I learned an important lesson about the true meaning of “Moscow rules”? Probably not.) Regardless, it’s a welcome comeback for a beloved character, despite her only appearing in literally three episodes of Season 1, and it added a fun last flourish to an episode that was already cruising.

As one slow horse enters the picture, another one leaves — poor Moira (Joanna Scanlan) was crossed off the list of the mysterious killers (Kyle Soller and MyAnna Buring). She may have escaped Slough House, but the asterisk on her file would never be deleted. Though we still know very little about who this duo is and why they’re taking out agents who might as well be dead to the Park, something is obviously off. “Seems too easy,” says Buring’s character. “Are you sure we have the right list?” At least now Coe (Tom Brooke) and Shirley (Aimee-Ffion Edwards), in their unlikely yet effective team-up, have picked up the pair’s scent after investigating the house boat of their dead colleague. Even though we’re supposed to hate this horse-murdering pair, their brief characterization across these two episodes has done a ton to up their intrigue points — details like Buring being picky about the goopy soup she’d burn on Moira’s stovetop to cover up the murder and Soller holding Moira’s limp hand as he clicks through TV channels.

Slow Horses Season 6, Episode 2 - Images

This entire episode, “Daddy Issues,” is packed with moments like that — Jackson Lamb (Gary Oldman) barking at River; River mimicking shooting a projectile in the back of Roddy’s (Christopher Chung) head; Roddy talking about how bitcoin is about to “pop off”; Lamb teasing the Park archivist (Parchivist?) Molly (Naomi Wirthner) about her slay-queen, glam-rock outfit. Actually, this episode was especially stuffed with zesty Lambisms. Taking these extra beats to add a punchline to deeply serious situations is part of the Slow Horses appeal, and Season 6 has once again demonstrated that this is the house style, not something that left with show creator Will Smith after Season 5.

Speaking of deeply serious: We now know that River’s dad Frank Harkness (Hugo Weaving) is maybe at least somewhat involved with the Slough House erasure at the Park, commissioning (and then killing) the Dog who nabbed those files from the records archive. But he’s left a witness, presumed to be a kid, to the murder and has the go-ahead to take care of it. Meanwhile, Diana Taverner (Kristin Scott Thomas) is not having the best time as First Chair now that she knows where the money she accepted from Peter Judd (Samuel West) came from and was blackmailed into a sit-down TV interview with the “very slightly right-leaning,” as Judd undersells it, news outlet Talkpoint. (Was that the first time we’ve ever seen Diana caught totally flat-footed?)

“Daddy Issues” is yet another Slow Horses episode that makes spinning a bunch of carefully managed plates look easy. But I’m cognizant of the time crunch; Season 6 has already burned through two episodes, and for as exciting as they are, all of these blank spots need to be filled in so that this web of intrigue doesn’t end in a jumbled mess.
